key_insight: Re-Search turns research ideation into a Twenty Questions–style game: an LLM receives a published paper’s research problem and asks yes-or-no questions to rediscover its core idea. This makes the model’s step-by-step search visible rather than evaluating only its final proposal.
problem_solved: Existing evaluations obscure how LLMs explore and refine research ideas, making it difficult to identify what limits their progress.
method: Give a model only the research problem from a published paper, withholding the paper’s core idea.
Use a two-player questioning game in which the model asks yes-or-no questions to narrow down possible ideas.
Examine the questioning trajectory to study iterative ideation. The provided abstract is truncated and does not include complete dataset details or results.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, Re-Search offers a way to inspect how models seek information and refine research hypotheses. It could support more diagnostic evaluations of research assistants, beyond judging their final outputs.
visual_elements: Two-player dialogue diagram showing an LLM asking questions and receiving yes-or-no feedback.
Branching decision tree illustrating how answers narrow the space of possible research ideas.
Step-by-step flow: research problem → questions → feedback → reconstructed core idea.
Side-by-side comparison of final-output evaluation and search-process evaluation.
paper_title: Re-Search: Dissecting LLM Ideation Through a Two-Player Questioning Game
paper_authors: Muhan Gao, Hangxiao Zhu, Xinqi Su, Yu Zhang, Daniel Khashabi
